rationale.conceptual: The method is an established quantum chemistry protocol (B3LYP/6-311G GIAO) that requires non-trivial knowledge of DFT, basis sets, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and conversion of shielding to chemical shifts. While not novel, correctly building four molecular structures, choosing appropriate software settings, and interpreting results demands careful implementation beyond a simple textbook example.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has three main stages (geometry optimization, NMR shielding, shift conversion) with dependencies on a specific quantum chemistry package. Setting up the environment, running multiple DFT jobs, extracting shieldings, and formatting the output requires moderate orchestration and handling of tool outputs, though the total number of steps is not excessive.
